questions.q: Which climate category does the Court give for Germany's wine regions as a whole?
questions.exp: Germany's vineyards lie between about 47 and 52 degrees north, at the cool edge of the wine world, with cold winters and warm but short growing seasons, so the Court calls the climate cool continental. Rivers and steep south-facing slopes supply the warmth the latitude lacks; moderate continental is the Court's word for Hungary, not Germany.

questions.q: Which German label term means noble rot, the botrytis behind Beerenauslese and Trockenbeerenauslese?
questions.exp: Edelfäule, literally noble rot, is the German word for Botrytis cinerea when it shrivels ripe, healthy grapes in a misty autumn and concentrates their sugar and acid. It is the source of most Beerenauslese and Trockenbeerenauslese; Eiswein reaches the same must weight by frost instead, with no botrytis at all.

questions.q: Schloss, German for castle, is the counterpart on a German label of which French word?
questions.exp: Schloss names a castle estate just as château does in Bordeaux, and the Rheingau holds the famous pair: Schloss Johannisberg, with its Spätlese legend of 1775, and Schloss Vollrads at Winkel. Both are Ortsteile, so their labels may carry the estate name without a village name in front of it. Domaine answers instead to Weingut, the plain wine estate.

questions.q: Dönnhoff, one of the estates the Court names among Germany's producers, is the reference house of which Anbaugebiet?
questions.exp: Dönnhoff farms the Brücke at Oberhausen, the Hermannshöhle at Niederhausen and the Kupfergrube, and its Riesling, from dry Grosses Gewächs to Eiswein, put the Nahe on the world's lists. The Court's other names place Hans Wirsching in Franken, Robert Weil, Künstler and Leitz in the Rheingau, Gunderloch in Rheinhessen and Joh. Jos. Prüm, Fritz Haag and Selbach-Oster on the Mosel.

questions.q: The German Wine Law of 1971 set up two top categories of wine, and one of them was QbA. Name the other.
questions.exp: The 1971 law made ripeness at harvest the measure of quality: QbA, Qualitätswein bestimmter Anbaugebiete, was quality wine from a named region that could be chaptalised, and QmP, Qualitätswein mit Prädikat, was the riper wine that could not. QmP was renamed Prädikatswein in 2007, the name the label carries today, with the same six Prädikate.

questions.q: Which Anbaugebiet does the Court name as Germany's largest, both in vineyard area and in the volume of wine it makes?
questions.exp: Rheinhessen, the rolling country inside the bend of the Rhine between Mainz, Worms and Bingen, is the largest of the thirteen regions by area and by output, and the Court lists Riesling as its grape, though Müller-Thurgau, Silvaner and Dornfelder are widely grown there too. The Pfalz to its south is second in size and Württemberg comes after Baden, while the Mosel, for all its fame, is far smaller.

questions.q: By the Court's definition, from which grapes must Deutscher Sekt be made?
opts: Grapes grown anywhere in the EU
questions.exp: Deutscher Sekt is sparkling wine from German grapes, made by any method, tank or bottle. A label that reads simply Sekt may be made from base wine grown anywhere in the European Union, while Sekt b.A. must come wholly from one of the thirteen Anbaugebiete and name it, and Riesling is common but never required.

questions.q: A wine list is arranged by style. Where does a Riesling Beerenauslese belong on it?
questions.exp: The Court describes Beerenauslese as very sweet and often touched by botrytis, so it sits with the dessert wines beside Trockenbeerenauslese and Eiswein, poured in small measures and served well chilled. Trocken wines join the crisp dry whites, and Kabinett and Spätlese, off-dry in their classic form, sit with the off-dry and aromatic whites.

questions.q: A guest orders pan-fried trout with brown butter and almonds and asks for a German Riesling. Which style suits the dish best?
questions.exp: Dry Riesling has the acidity to cut brown butter and the delicacy to leave river fish intact, the same reasoning that makes it a partner for pork, roast chicken and asparagus. The very sweet styles belong with foie gras, blue cheese and fruit desserts, and off-dry Kabinett or Spätlese is the answer for chilli heat and spice.
